title: Head, Office of the CPCO
description: THE OPPORTUNITY This role combines advisory support with high-level executive coordination to ensure the seamless functioning of the Office of the CPCO . The incumbent will play a pivotal role in managing the CPCO’s office operations, driving strategic priorities, and enabling effective internal and external engagement. As both a trusted advisor and executive partner, this individual ensures organizational alignment, timely execution of high-impact initiatives, and thoughtful management of the CPCO’s time and influence. They will also provide proactive administrative and communications support, enhancing the CPCO ’s capacity to lead the People and Culture function. WAYS YOU CAN CONTRIBUTE Partner with the CPCO to track and drive progress on strategic initiatives and leadership priorities. Partner with the Chief P&C Officer (CPCO) to track and drive progress on strategic priorities, leadership commitments, and key P&C initiatives. Conduct research, synthesize information, and provide insights and recommendations to support the CPCO’s decision-making. Prepare high-quality briefing materials, talking points, presentations, and recommendations for internal and external engagements. Provide proactive insights and timely updates on emerging priorities, risks, and matters requiring the CPCO’s attention or intervention. Support the translation of P&C strategic priorities into coordinated plans and priorities across the function. Drive alignment and coordination across the P&C Leadership Team, ensuring connectivity across priorities, dependencies, and deliverables. Coordinate cross-functional efforts on priorities requiring collaboration between P&C and other functions or delivery platforms across the Foundation. Monitor progress against P&C strategic and operational priorities, identify risks and dependencies, and drive appropriate follow-through and accountability. Coordinate materials, briefings, and preparation for Executive Committee, Board, P&C Leadership Team, and other executive-level meetings and engagements. Support the development and dissemination of communications, updates, and key messages from the CPCO’s Office. Oversee the effective functioning of the CPCO’s Office, ensuring priorities, meetings, engagements, and follow-up actions are effectively coordinated. Serve as a key liaison between the CPCO and senior internal and external stakeholders, facilitating timely communication, alignment, and follow-through. Manage sensitive and confidential matters on behalf of the CPCO with sound judgment, discretion, and professionalism. Lead the planning and delivery of special initiatives and cross-functional projects sponsored by the CPCO. Support the CPCO in identifying opportunities to strengthen P&C effectiveness, integration, ways of working, and delivery against organizational priorities. WHO YOU ARE Bachelor’s degree required PMI certified Member of a relevant professional body. 1 0 years of progressive experience supporting senior executives, ideally in a complex, matrixed organization. Experience handling sensitive and confidential matters and engaging effectively with senior leadership, Board-level stakeholders, and external partners. Proven ability to navigate matrixed environments and align cross-functional teams to strategic goals. Experience driving strategic planning, execution tracking, and follow-through across a large or complex function. Ability to contribute to the development of functional strategy, translate strategic direction into priorities and plans, and support effective execution and monitoring. Advanced use of tools such as Microsoft Office, Asana, SharePoint, and other coordination platforms. Strong ability to lead complex, cross-functional initiatives, manage interdependencies, and establish mechanisms for tracking delivery, risks, and accountability. Ability to navigate complex stakeholder environments, facilitate alignment, and coordinate effectively across functions and leadership teams. Demonstrates sound judgment, emotional intelligence, and discretion. Exceptional communication and relationship management skills. Values kindness, respect, and inclusive collaboration. Comfortable managing competing priorities with calm, efficiency, and flexibility. Operates with integrity, attention to detail, and service-oriented mindset. The Mastercard Foundation values the unique skills and experiences each individual brings to the organization and we are committed to creating and maintaining an inclusive and accessible environment for everyone. Completion of satisfactory business references and background checks are essential conditions of employment. For more information and to sign up for the Foundation’s newsletter, please visit http://www.mastercardfdn.org/ Follow the Foundation on Twitter at MastercardFdn

title: Lead, Pandemic Sciences
description: THE OPPORTUNITY Reporting to the Director, Higher Education, Health Collaboratives, the Lead, Pandemic Sciences will be responsible for engaging partners and youth to drive the successful implementation of the Foundations Health Collaboratives namely the Pandemic Sciences Collaborative as well the Public Health and Primary Health Care Collaborative. The role builds and stewards high-quality partnerships that advance youth-centred health programming across Africa. WAYS YOU CAN CONTRIBUTE Partnership design and delivery Contribute to the design and implementation of the Higher Education Pandemic Sciences Collaborative. Co-create proposals with prospective partners across the respective collaboratives. Collaborate with colleagues across the Foundation teams to strengthen new and existing partnerships. Advise and accompany partners on implementation, progress tracking, and learning, ensuring high-quality delivery across the partnership portfolio. Support the planning and execution of governance structures within the collaboratives. Convening, learning and reporting Organize monthly or quarterly partner meetings to ensure excellence in implementation. Plan and deliver face-to-face convenings and virtual meetings. Capture data and learnings, ensuring insights and impact are routinely and effectively reported and integrated into program adaptations. Analyze and synthesize partner feedback to inform broader program development and drive continuous improvement. Support connections, exchange, and learning across the regional portfolio. Stakeholder management and safeguarding Cultivate and manage relationships with stakeholders to scale impact. Support partners in safeguarding the wellbeing of all program participants. Health Workforce Initiatives Support translation of the Foundation’s Health Workforce Initiatives strategy into operational plans and program delivery across countries. Lead day-to-day implementation of Health Workforce portfolios, ensuring program quality, timelines, and measurable outcomes. Provide technical expertise on Health Workforce Initiatives models, supervision systems, and workforce retention. Coordinate implementing partners to strengthen operational efficiency and service integration . WHO YOU ARE Academic & Professional Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Health related field , p ublic p olicy, i nternational d evelopment, s ocial s ciences or related field from a recognized university. Masters degree in a Health related field is an asset. Relevant professional qualification. Experience Minimum of ten ( 10 ) years’ relevant experience in a similar settings. E xperience in e ngaging with faculty/staff in higher education institutions, civil society organizations, government, private sector etc., as well as young people. Managing multiple projects and delivering results in a fast-paced and fluid environment. Experience in designing and delivering health, science and/or leadership development programs for young people, in Africa. Experience with global grant making. Experience working across cultures and geographies, living and working in Africa is highly desirable Competencies Fluent in English and relevant local languages. Knowledge of health education and youth employment issues in Africa. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Experience with inclusion and marginalized youth. Strong interpersonal and partnership-building skills, with excellent communication and presentation abilities. Team player with high emotional intelligence. Entrepreneurial mindset with a service orientation aligned with Foundation values. Results-driven, with a sense of urgency and ability to manage multiple priorities in fast-paced environments. Ability to balance execution with longer-term planning. Commitment to youth empowerment and inclusion, and to innovation, co-creation, humility, and learning. The Mastercard Foundation values the unique skills and experiences each individual brings to the organization and we are committed to creating and maintaining an inclusive and accessible environment for everyone. Completion of satisfactory business references and background checks are essential conditions of employment.
